title: The iPhone Duo’s battery life is better than you might expect

 Devices Handsets News Syndication The iPhone Duo’s battery life is better than you might expect
 By Tyler Lee 
 2 days ago 
 0 
 Battery life is one of those things we tend to take for granted until that dreaded low battery warning pops up. Foldables have it tougher, since there’s a bigger screen to power. So when Apple launched the iPhone Duo with its 7.6-inch inner display, battery life was one of the bigger question marks. Now, we have a better idea of how it holds up.

 iPhone 18 Pro Max wins PhoneBuff’s latest battery test
 In a new video (see below), PhoneBuff put several iPhones running iOS 27 through a series of everyday tasks. These included phone calls, messaging, email, web browsing, Instagram, YouTube, gaming, GPS navigation, Spotify and standby. To keep things fair, every display was calibrated to 200 nits and the speakers were set to the same volume.
 Unsurprisingly, the iPhone 18 Pro Max came out on top, lasting 30 hours and 13 minutes. Interestingly enough, the iPhone Duo put up a pretty respectable fight. It fell behind the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, but it outlasted the iPhone 17 and the iPhone Air. Considering its two batteries add up to 4,883mAh, which is less than the Pro Max’s 5,567mAh , that’s not too shabby.
 As for the iPhone 17 and the ultra-thin iPhone Air, they were the first to call it quits, with the Air narrowly edging out the 17. There’s only so much battery you can squeeze into a phone that thin, after all.
 Keep it closed if you can
 During the GPS navigation test, closing the Duo and sticking to the outer display helped stretch its battery life a lot. On the flip side, opening it up created a noticeable drain. Display size and speaker quality also proved to be major factors in power consumption across the board.
 Basically, if you want the most battery life out of the Duo, the outer screen is your friend. That being said, buying a $1,999 foldable and never unfolding it kind of defeats the purpose.
 We should also note that results depend on how a test is run. Case in point, a battery test by Tom’s Guide that had the phones browse the web over 5G saw the Duo last 13 hours and 20 minutes, while the Pro Max hit 17 hours and 31 minutes.
 Either way, if battery life is your top priority, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is still the one to beat. However, if you’ve got your heart set on the Duo, battery life shouldn’t be a dealbreaker.
